title: The portability check flags the {/< escapes its own message recommends, because it scans decoded text nodes
description:
FOUND IN THE FIELD by opum-doc (lore 0.12.0, measured 2026-10-01 02:50Z on its branch docs/ODOC-364-ripgrep-research), relayed by opum-agent; INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED here 2026-10-01 on a fixture of my own, dev source and released 0.12.0 identical.

THE DEFECT. mdxHazardFindings (src/core/check.ts, ~line 1436) warns when a mdast **text** node's value contains a raw `<` or `{`. mdast decodes character references into text-node values, so a source `{` arrives decoded as `{` and is flagged; likewise `<`. The finding's own message says "escape it ({) or wrap the text in backticks" -- and the FIRST of those two remedies does not clear the warning. Only backticks do.

FIXTURE (temp bundle, one file per shape; source binary and released 0.12.0 identical):
  probe/raw-brace.md       "A raw { brace in prose."                    -> warns (correct control)
  probe/backtick-brace.md  "A backticked `{` brace."                    -> no warning (correct control)
  probe/escaped-brace.md   "An escaped { brace in prose."          -> WARNS (wrong: the recommended escape)
  probe/escaped-angle.md   "An escaped < angle in prose."            -> WARNS (wrong)
  probe/escaped-plain.md   "The tools are {grep, ag, ...}"    -> WARNS (wrong; the field shape)
  probe/escaped-in-link.md "[{grep, ag, git grep}](https://example.com/)" -> WARNS (wrong; the field shape)

WHY IT MATTERS. In MDX it is the source-level `{` that starts a JSX expression, and character references are decoded after parsing, so `{` in source is portable -- the warned documents are fine to ship, and the check contradicts the portable subset its own message names. `lore check --strict` fails on them, so an author who follows the message escapes and stays red, or restructures correct prose. One of the two is wrong and it is the flag, not the message.

CLASSIFICATION: a reproducible defect -- the tool contradicts its own documented behaviour, the remedy it prints.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fixture whose only `<`/`{` occurrences are character references -- in prose and inside link text -- produces no portability finding, while raw `<`/`{` in prose still warns; both controls live in the same case, so a mutation that stops flagging raw characters is red too.
Both remedies the finding message names actually clear the warning: escaping (`{`/`<`) and backticks, asserted for each of the two characters.
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.
